sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Type checking rules
sections.what: Turns on strict type checking and sets the @ shortcut for project files.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes imports shorter and catches mistakes early.
sections.watch_out: Strict mode can turn small type slips into build failures.

summary: Sets the TypeScript rules for the frontend, including strict checking and a short @ path for project files.
purpose: Controls how strictly the code is checked and how imports are found.
why: Likely reason: strict checking catches many bugs before the app runs.
how: Sets the output target, the library list, strict checks, the Next.js plugin, and an @ alias that points to the project root.
inputs: The TypeScript files in the frontend.
outputs: Type check results during the build or while editing.
risks: With strict checks on, a type error can stop the build. The @ alias must match the folder layout.
debug: If an import using @ fails, check that the alias points to the project root. If the build stops on type errors, read the first error message.
